subject: Accounting
title: CEO Certification
description: A short lesson to help you apply CEO Certification.

hook.text: After Sarbanes-Oxley, CEOs must personally sign off on financial statements. False certification means prison.

buildup.text: Section 302 requires the CEO and CFO to certify that financial reports are accurate and complete.

discovery.text: Section 906 adds criminal penalties: up to $5 million in fines and 20 years for knowing violations.

twist.text: The idea is simple—executives can no longer claim they 'didn't know' about accounting problems.

climax.text: Personal accountability has made top executives far more engaged in financial reporting processes.

punchline.text: Sign your name. Own the numbers. Face the consequences.

quiz.question: What does SOX Section 302 require?
options: CEO and CFO to personally certify financial reports
All employees to review the annual report
External auditors to guarantee zero errors

details.summary: CEO certification requires chief executives to personally vouch for the accuracy of financial statements. Introduced by Sarbanes-Oxley, it creates personal accountability at the top and carries criminal penalties for false certification.
details.whyItMatters: Before CEO certification, executives could claim ignorance of fraudulent reporting. Personal liability changed the calculus, making leaders directly responsible for financial accuracy.
takeaways: Sarbanes-Oxley Section 302 requires CEO and CFO certification of all financial reports
False certification can result in fines up to $5 million and 20 years in prison
CEO certification drove companies to strengthen internal controls and review processes

faq.question: What is CEO certification under Sarbanes-Oxley?
faq.answer: CEO certification, required by SOX Section 302, mandates that CEOs and CFOs personally sign off on the accuracy and completeness of financial reports filed with the SEC, making them legally liable for any material misstatements.

faq.question: What are the penalties for false CEO certification?
faq.answer: Under SOX Section 906, executives who knowingly certify false financial statements face fines up to $5 million and up to 20 years in prison. Even negligent certification carries significant civil penalties.
